main_body: Two-storey half-timbered house with a large hipped tile roof, a cream plaster upper wall with timber frame, a cobblestone ground floor, a wooden door and a hanging sign
top_band: Roof slope in orange and red tiles with a light ridge highlight, rows 4-43 at x=48. The tiles alternate between mid-light orange and dark maroon. The hip slopes on the left and right are also visible.
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface seen from above, with hip planes at both ends and a ridge highlight. It ends in a clear eave line with a dark shadow band at rows 44-45 above the wall. Below it is the vertical front face, with timber framing, inset windows with sills and flower boxes, a cobblestone base and a door. This matches the construction of the reference houses, so the roof reads as a top surface and the wall as a separate front face.

style.evidence: The candidate has 19 median colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0% and it has 191 distinct colours. Only 12% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted (dark maroon beside the roof, dark brown beside timber). The roof tiles carry per-tile highlights. The plaster is speckled and the cobblestones are shaded one by one. The timber and the window glass also have several steps. It sits at the level of the references.
